result.title: Meta-memorization and memorization scaling laws in transformers
result.summary: Larger transformers can memorize more data, with a capacity (in bits) that scales roughly linearly with the number of parameters. Counterintuitively, larger models also memorize faster, requiring fewer repetitions of a sequence during training before it is memorized. We reproduce both memorization scaling laws in transformers trained on random binary sequences, showing that rapid memorization can arise even when data contain no semantic or compositional structure. Rapid memorization is due to a meta-memorization effect, where models trained to memorize a large set of random sequences learn to memorize novel sequences more quickly. The rate $r(t)$ at which models memorize grows with training time $t$ as a power-law $r(t) \sim t^β$ with a fixed exponent $β$ but an increasing upper cutoff across model scales. Meta-memorization enables even one-layer transformers to few-shot memorize a 100-bit sequence. This effect is partly explained by the formation of structured attention heads that convey position-invariant sequence information to MLPs where memorized sequences are stored. Meta-memorization is recapitulated in a simplified model of a dense associative memory where retrieval is constrained by an attentional bottleneck. Our results suggest transformers, through pre-training, acquire reusable mechanisms that enable highly efficient storage and retrieval of memories.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在随机二值序列上复现记忆容量与记忆速度的缩放律，提出「元记忆」效应：模型在大规模随机序列训练中学会更快记忆新序列，并将其部分归因于结构化注意力头向 MLP 传递位置无关的序列信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 「结构化注意力头 + MLP 存储」与「注意力瓶颈约束检索」的机制可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的读写路径、位置无关内容与深度/位置对表示相似度的影响，以及瓶颈带来的信息压缩；纯文本随机序列任务与视觉推理本身无直接关联。
